title: pgAdmin 4 AI Assistant -- T1059 multi-statement READ ONLY transaction bypass
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-12045 (CVSS 9.4 CRITICAL), a
read-only-transaction bypass in pgAdmin 4's AI Assistant, affecting
versions 9.13 through 9.16 (fixed in 9.16, commit `bf4792444`).

The AI Assistant's `execute_sql_query` tool runs LLM-generated SQL
inside a `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY` wrapper specifically to prevent
data modification. The LLM-supplied query, however, was forwarded to the
database driver without being restricted to a single statement or to
read-only verbs. A multi-statement payload beginning with a
transaction-control keyword (`COMMIT`, `END`, `ROLLBACK`, or `ABORT`)
terminates the wrapping READ ONLY transaction early; every statement
after it then runs in ordinary autocommit mode, and the trailing
`ROLLBACK` the wrapper issues at the end has no effect since the
transaction it was meant to roll back is already gone. Delivery is via
prompt injection: content the AI Assistant later reads (a row, a column
value, a comment) can steer the LLM into emitting exactly this
multi-statement shape as its tool call. With ordinary write privileges
this yields unauthorized data modification; with a superuser role or
`pg_execute_server_program`, the chain extends to RCE via
`COPY ... TO PROGRAM`.

Detection logic flags the specific structural signature the fix's own
validation targets: a query submitted to `execute_sql_query` that is NOT
a single, non-empty statement whose leading token is one of
`SELECT`/`WITH`/`EXPLAIN`/`SHOW`/`VALUES`/`TABLE` -- concretely, one
containing a transaction-control keyword anywhere before a trailing
write statement, rather than as the query's own sole content.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor disclosure (pgAdmin project, via
the public GitHub issue and fix commit), fixed in 9.16.
